learning_outcomes.text: The student/graduate uses basic concepts, models, and theories from the fundamental and engineering sciences to solve problems specific to heat and mass transfer.
The student/graduate analyzes simple engineering products, processes, and systems using analytical, numerical, and experimental methods, new or innovative, and interprets the results.
The student/graduate chooses and applies appropriate and relevant methods to identify, formulate, and solve incompletely defined engineering problems in the field of heat and mass transfer.
The student/graduate chooses and applies design methods (including computer-aided design) and/or their own creativity for the development of new and complex products, processes, and systems.

The student/graduate uses available information sources (scientific databases, digital resources on the internet) to identify, locate, and obtain necessary data for bibliographic studies, to perform simulations and modeling.

The student/graduate understands and applies standards and regulations specific to engineering practice, analysis, design, and research techniques and methods, including computer usage, for solving problems or realizing applied engineering projects in the field of heat and mass transfer in buildings.
The student/graduate uses digital tools for presenting heat and mass transfer works.
The student/graduate understands the use of different measurement and evaluation methods.
The student/graduate operates laboratory equipment used for characterizing and evaluating heat and mass transfer parameters, for each type individually or combined.
The student/graduate critically evaluates processes, equipment, procedures, and products from the field of thermal sciences using specific evaluation instruments and methods.

The student/graduate respects ethical principles, norms, and values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks, by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in decision-making for problem-solving.
The student/graduate integrates into the workgroup and applies effective relational and work techniques in multidisciplinary teams, at various hierarchical levels.
The student/graduate continuously informs and documents themselves in their field of activity by adequately using efficient lifelong learning methods and techniques.
The student/graduate elaborates professional projects in the field of engineering.

syllabus_topics: Analogies between momentum, heat, and mass transfer
Convective heat transfer in forced external and internal flow
Ideal and real radiative heat exchange
Occupational safety notions in the laboratory. Error analysis.
One-dimensional conduction in extended surfaces (long rods)
Retake lab sessions. Submission of lab reports
Heat transfer through building elements. Energy audit
Calculation of heat losses (thermal transfer) STAS, specialized software
Sizing of heating and domestic hot water preparation system
teaching_methods: Debates based on Power Point presentations
Direct and indirect exploration of reality (experiment, demonstration, modeling)

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory activity (completion of lab sheets and evaluation test)
Project (design activity, project finalization, project presentation)

assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Whole grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with grade 5 certifying the acquisition of minimal learning outcomes for a discipline and the award of corresponding study credits. A minimum score of 5 is required for the exam component, laboratory activity, and project to pass.
